name: GSA SAM.gov landing page: federal contracting notices
title: GSA SAM.gov landing page: federal contracting notices
answer: SAM.gov is a U.S. General Services Administration federal government computer system and landing page for federal contracting information. The most useful thing it says for this reader is that FPDS.gov ezSearch has been retired and users should conduct all contract awards data searches in SAM.gov, with the FPDS.gov ATOM Feed to be retired later in FY 2026. The page itself is mostly operational notices about wage determinations, subcontracting reporting, and system use, not an AI or Defense analysis.

sections.body: SAM.gov is published by the U.S. General Services Administration, which describes the site as a federal government computer system for official use only. The harvested text is a landing page, not a report or article. It carries a set of operational notices, including one dated June 9, 2026, and others dated 4/29/2026 and 04/29/2026. No publication date is stated for the page itself. Its scope is federal contracting systems and administrative updates, with no stated focus on artificial intelligence or the Defense industry.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The page carries operational notices rather than analysis. It says revisions to ISR eligibility logic in the Subcontracting Plan Reporting system took effect on June 9, 2026, and contractors might see more contracts and subcontracts in their Eligible Workspace, though the sentence is cut off. It notes that wage determination formatting on SAM.gov has changed and gives contacts for construction Davis-Bacon and service Service Contract Act questions. It warns that some SCA Wage Determinations published on 4/29/2026 may have incomplete location information and asks users who see a discrepancy with the previous revision to submit an e98 request. It states that Executive Order 13658 generally applies to contracts under the Service Contract Act or Davis-Bacon Act awarded between January 1, 2015, and January 29, 2022, and not renewed or extended on or after January 30, 2022, and sets a minimum wage of $13.65 per hour, with the sentence cut off. It announces that FPDS.gov ezSearch has been retired and that all contract awards data searches should be conducted in SAM.gov, and that the FPDS.gov ATOM Feed will be retired later in FY 2026. It also states that the system is a GSA Federal Government computer system for official use only, subject to monitoring, that unauthorized activities can lead to disciplinary action including criminal prosecution, and that the system contains Controlled Unclassified Information to be protected under 32 CFR Part 2002 and GSA Order CIO 2103.2 CUI Policy.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The source states that ISR eligibility logic revisions took effect on June 9, 2026. It gives 4/29/2026 and 04/29/2026 as dates for SCA Wage Determination issues. It says EO 13658 applies to contracts awarded between January 1, 2015, and January 29, 2022, and not renewed or extended on or after January 30, 2022, and sets a minimum wage of $13.65 per hour. It states that FPDS.gov ezSearch has been retired and the FPDS.gov ATOM Feed will be retired later in FY 2026. It says the system contains Controlled Unclassified Information and cites 32 CFR Part 2002 and GSA Order CIO 2103.2 CUI Policy.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in Defense would use this source only as a system notice about where federal contract award data searches are moving. The text says FPDS.gov ezSearch has been retired and users should conduct all contract awards data searches in SAM.gov, and that the FPDS.gov ATOM Feed will be retired later in FY 2026. It does not name any AI-related DoD solicitation, award, or vendor registration, so it supports the claim that SAM.gov is a federal contracting system, not a source of AI analysis.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Defense

sections.body: The harvested text is a landing page with truncated notices, not a full document. It does not mention artificial intelligence, the Defense industry, DoD solicitations, awards, or vendor registrations. Several sentences are cut off, including the ISR eligibility notice and the EO 13658 minimum wage sentence. It gives no publication date for the page itself. It is a government system page, not commercial analysis, and its content is administrative and operational. It is partial because the source text is a harvest of selected notices, not the full SAM.gov site or search results.
